To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a hydrophilic PVP pore-former blended polyethersulfonesulfone UF membrane can be successfully synthesized via the wet-phase inversion technique.

the addition of 1 wt%, 10 wt%, or 20 wt % of PVP to a polyethersulfonate ultrafiltration membrane can significantly improve membrane flux, and that the membrane containing 10 wt % PVP showed the highest flux recovery ratio during humic acid filtration.

(1) the addition of PVP as a hydrophilic additive can improve the performance of polyethersulfones UF membranes, (2) the addition of 20 wt.% PVP can increase membrane pure water permeation to 2400 Lm−2h−1bar−1, and (3) the addition of a small amount of PVP can reduce the membrane fouling by humic acids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel UF membrane that can be applied in the treatment of wastewater for water reuse.
the development of a hydrophilic PVP-polyethersulfone blend membrane that has high water permeation, high humic acid rejection, and excellent fouling resistance.

the effect of extremely high PVP concentrations on the properties of polyethersulfones, and the results are expected to contribute to the development of novel UF membranes that are more resistant to humic acid fouls.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the addition of PVP, up to 10 wt%, is recommended considering cleaning frequency and moderately high flux during fouling for field application in water treatment processes.
the optimum concentration of PVP for humic acid filtration is 10 wt%.
the addition of a proper concentration of a hydrophilic additive, PVP, can improve the membrane performance and reduce fouling in terms of flux and rejection of humic substances.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of 20 wt%-PVP to PES membranes can improve the permeability and selectivities of the membranes without sacrificing humic substances rejection.
the addition of PVP can be an effective strategy to mitigate humic acid fouled UF membranes.
the addition of a hydrophilic additive to a membrane can improve membrane fouling resistance, and the optimum hydrophilic additive concentration should be carefully selected for each application.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a very small addition of PVP (1 wt%) to the polyethersulfones solution can significantly increase membrane flux and selectivity, and the addition of PVP up to a concentration of 10 % significantly improves the fouling resistance of polyethersulfonate membranes during humic acid filtration, while 20 wt % PVP addition decreases the membrane flux and selectivities.

a small addition of hydrophilic PVP to polyethersulfones membranes can significantly improve the membrane's performance in terms of humic acid rejection and flux recovery ratio, while maintaining the membrane's selectivity.
the use of extremely high concentrations of PVP as pore-former can significantly improve membrane fouling by humic acid.
